title: Orchestrator → pool quota propagation gap caused large request latency spikes and customer escalations
creator: Anita Gomez
description: Summary: Between 2026-03-10 03:45 and 2026-03-10 08:20 UTC several customers on Hosted and Dedicated tiers experienced large request latency spikes and stream truncation. Root cause was a propagation/scheme mismatch between the orchestrator's new quota warmup semantics and the per-pool admission controller used by dedicated/private runtime agents. The mismatch caused admission controllers to treat requests as 'defer' and hold them indefinitely until downstream compute timeouts, producing customer-facing 504s, stalled streams, and elevated token billing anomalies. One enterprise customer raised an urgent escalation impacting production features.
repro_steps: Deploy runtime-1.21 feature flag for 'quota-warmup-v2' to orchestrator only (simulate rollout)
Send steady ramp traffic with short bursts and high token variance (seq len 512 to 4096)
Observe orchestrator accepting requests but per-pool admission controller applying legacy epoch semantics that allocate zero immediate credit during warmup
Measure long in-flight request queues on dedicated GPU pool nodes and backend compute timeouts leading to 504s and truncated streaming responses
investigation_notes: 03:50 UTC - PagerDuty alerts: spike in 504s and kernel compute timeouts for pools in us-west1, eu-west1
04:05 UTC - Identified correlation: alerts only for routes using new rate-profile 'burst-aware-v2' that had been enabled in the control plane earlier that morning
04:18 UTC - Rolling restart of runtime agents on two dedicated pools temporarily reduced spike but issue reappeared for private deployments where agents are customer-managed

04:45 UTC - Captured admission logs showing 'warmup_credit==0' while orchestrator metrics showed consumed_quota>0; discovered serialization version mismatch in quota epoch header between orchestrator (v2) and agent (v1)
05:10 UTC - Customer Ops notified enterprise customer (billing & SRE) and provided first mitigation ETA

05:35 UTC - Observed token-metering discrepancy where orchestrator persisted a request acceptance but compute nodes never started decoding tensors in some cases, causing duplicate billed but unserved attempts
mitigation: Immediate: Disabled 'quota-warmup-v2' rollout flag in control plane at 05:50 UTC to force back-compat behavior
Immediate: Issued orchestration policy reload to all edge proxies and accelerated config refresh for dedicated pools
Customer communication: Sent incident update to impacted accounts with recommended client-side retry/backoff until 08:20 UTC
Hotfix: Deployed runtime-1.21.3 to orchestrator and rolled as a compatibility shim to accept both v1 and v2 epoch headers at 07:30 UTC
root_cause: A backwards-incompatible change to quota warmup semantics (epoch header format and interpretation) was rolled to the orchestrator before the dedicated/private runtime agents had an updated deserialization handler. This caused per-pool admission controllers to compute zero warmup credit and queue requests until backend compute timeouts, resulting in customer-visible latency, 504s, and stream truncation.
fixes: Backported compatibility parser to runtime agents so they accept both epoch formats (PR #12487)
Added a control-plane rollout gate that prevents enabling new epoch semantics unless all active agent versions report readiness
Implemented end-to-end CI that runs orchestrator + agent compatibility matrix for quota header evolution
Added alert: 'quota-propagation-mismatch' that trips when orchestrator-accepted requests exceed per-pool admission throughput for >2m
Improved logging: include epoch header version and agent binary version in admission log lines
postmortem_followup: ENG: Add periodic agent-version inventory check to deployment pipeline (owner: infra-team)
PM: Update rollout checklist to require compatibility matrix sign-off before enabling control-plane flags
SRE: Create a synthetic load test that exercises warmup windows across sequence lengths and batch shapes
Billing: Audit the affected window for duplicate/incomplete billing events and reconcile with customers
DX: Add guidance to Console showing agent version skew and automated rollback option for risky flags
